recipes.name: Gourmet Microwave Popcorn
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon olive oil, or more if needed

steps.text: Place popcorn in a brown paper bag. Tightly seal the bag by folding the top several times.
Microwave on High until the popping slows, about 2 minutes. Carefully open the bag. Season with salt and drizzle with olive oil. Reclose the bag and shake to distribute the seasoning.

raw_recipe.headline: Gourmet Microwave Popcorn
raw_recipe.description: Make your own microwave popcorn. All you need is popcorn, olive oil, salt, and brown paper bag!

review.reviewBody: OMG - What a great recipe! This is so simple and so easy yet tastes so good! I've tried it with the olive oil (a little melted butter works great too), just watch your microwave times as everyone's microwaves are different. The possibilites are endless in terms of seasonings you can but on top - I've also kept it simple and light and just used butter spray! This is a great snack especially when you just want a little something to munch on... Definitely won't be going back to the pre-packaged stuff, sorry Mr. Redenbacher!

Yes, this is less expensive and healthier than the premade microwave popcorn bags and uses less oil than if popping on the stove. With this paper bag method you must be take care with the details & pay attention, in order to get a good final product and for safety. This paper bag method is best for small batches only, 1-2 servings. Use the brown paper lunch bags that come in a pack of 50-100 or so. Fold the 2 open ends together and over 2-3 times, make two little vertical tears in the folded portion, to create a small tab. Fold the tab over and this helps keep the bag closed. Watch the popping carefully the first few times, till you get the hang of the amount of time needed, the power of your microwave, etc. Once the popping slows to near stop, stop cooking immediately or it will burn or could start a fire. Some kernels will remain unpopped. Longer cooking may pop the rest, but will burn some of the already-popped kernels, so it is not recommended. Use caution when opening the finished bag as the hot steam can cause burns. Children should always be supervised by adults for this paper bag cooking method. I pour the popped corn into a bowl, drizzle with oil, sprinkle with salt, and then mix around. Garlic olive oil and finely grated parmesan cheese is a tasty topping.

I love the recipe! Olive oil popcorn with just a touch of salt and cracked pepper is great! I do follow this, but make this slightly different. I coat my kernels in olive oil before I place them in the bag. Then I drizzle a little olive oil on and toss with salt & pepper.

I love it so much that I got a special silicone 'microwave popper' to make it in! Add other seasonings, too, like lemon pepper, Italian seasoning with a bit of parmesan cheese, chili powder, 5 spice powder, or nutritional yeast. My Husband's favorite is to add5 spice powder with a little powdered wasabi. To make it more like theatre popcorn, substitute virgin coconut oil for the olive oil!

I've always made microwave popcorn using vegetable oil and salt all in the bag then pop in the microwave. I tried this tonight but I did not measure the oil or salt as I used Bertolli 100% extra virgin olive oil spray. After it popped I sprayed the olive oil in the bag and sprinkled some salt and closed the bag and shook it several times. I opened the bag and tasted and spayed a few more sprays of olive oil and shakes of salt and closed the bag and shook it a few times. This is how I will make it from now on! Yum!

So simple and no mess. I used a brown lunch bag and it took 2 minutes and 30 seconds in our microwave. A great method if you just want a small batch of popcorn. I also used this method to make 'Garlic Bread Popcorn' and 'Sriracha-Lime Popcorn' both from AR.

this recipe rules! i put it in my microwave for 2 min. 10 seconds and its perfect every time. Make sure you put the kernels and salt in first then sprinkle the oil over it or it will burn and the bag soaks up all of the oil.

No mess ... very economical to make and bags can be reused at least one other time depending what you add or don't add to your popcorn ... much healthier than commericial microwave popcorn because there are no artificial ingredients and the size was just right for a snack. Without any seasoning it taste like air-popped corn. I used a 10x5 brown bag and it was perfect. You have to be cautious when judging the time because you don't want to burn the popcorn that has already popped but you don't want too many "old maids" left behind. Every microwave is a little different but once you know your microwave's time it's a cinch!

No bag necessary! Just a large bowl and a plate over it worked for me. Couldent find a recepie for that so winging it off of the side of the container we came up with the same result, just with a ceramic bowl that will be HOT. Good stuff, skip the bag hunt and go for it!

Well, I don't know how to rate this recipe. The popcorn was popping, but I guess I should have known not to put the popcorn in a paper grocery bag that had print on it. As I took the bag out of the microwave, the bag caught on fire. If I try it again, I'll make sure it's a regular lunch paper bag.

I was planning on purchasing a popcorn popper since I no longer will be buying unhealthy pre-packaged microwave popcorn, but this method using a brown lunch bag works quite well. I need to play with the time as I had a lot of unpopped kernels. This method produced nicely popped popcorn without the added oil. Take a look at the ingredients in pre-packaged microwave popcorn. You’ll be glad you chose this method instead!
No changes.
It is really good. Although instead of olive oil I used vegetable oil spray and I just sprayed it a little bit before microwaving it.
We ditched the chemical laden pre-packaged microwave popcorn and now use this recipe. Living cleaner and loving this popcorn pop method.
Only way to make popcorn! And you can add whatever spices you like to customize it to your tastes. Perfect! Make sure you have plain paper bags. Any kind of print WILL make a difference!
Have started making it several times per week (up from once in a blue moon)!
Easy to make and so tasty! I transformed this for Halloween by making it sweet and salt by adding candy corn.
